chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Umar ibn Abi Bakkar, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad to Zuba'ah, daughter of Al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib. And he married him for the marriages to be humble/modest, and for them to follow the example of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and for them to know that the most noble of them in the sight of Allah is the most pious of them.

key_terms.الزُّبَيْرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَُطَّلِبِ: Al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib, uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.لِتَتَّضِعَ الْمَنَاكِحُ: For marriages to be humble/modest (not ostentatious)
key_terms.مِقْدَادَ بْنَ الْأَسْوَدِ: Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, a prominent companion

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet (SAWW) marry Miqdad to Zuba'ah and what does it teach about nobility in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi records the Prophet Muhammad's (SAW) marriage of Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad to Zuba'ah bint Al-Zubayr, a union that served as a practical lesson in humility (tadhi' al-manakih) for the community. Shia scholars emphasize this event to illustrate that the Prophet's marital choices were deliberate pedagogical acts, reinforcing the Quranic principle that true nobility lies in taqwa (piety) rather than lineage or wealth.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Umar Bin Abu Bakaar, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> got Miqdad Bin Al-Aswad<sup>as</sup> married to Zuba’at daughter of Al Zubeyr Bin Abdul Muttalib, and rather he<sup>saww</sup> got him<sup>as</sup> married in order to set the rules of the marriage and (for people) to follow the footsteps of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and to let them know that the most prestigious of them in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the most pious of them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Tha’Iabah ibn Maymun from ‘Umar ibn abu Bakkar from ibn abu Bakr af-Hadramiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, arranged a marriage between Miqdad ibn al-Aswad and Duba‘ah daughter of al-Zubayr ibn ‘ Abd al-Muttalib. He (the Messenger of Allah) did so only to explain the rules of marriage so that people follow the foot- steps of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and take notice that the most excellent in the sight of Allah are the most pious people.’”
